column1: # register-owners.tsv — WHO OUTSIDE THE HAL TOUCHES A GIME/MMU/SAM REGISTER.
# Checked by harness/tools/register_owner_check.py, wired into build.bat. A row is an
# OWNERSHIP fact: this file accesses this register. Adding an access to a register a file
# already owns is free; a NEW file, or a NEW register in an existing file, is a new row and
# FAILS THE BUILD until the row is added here.
# ★ ADDING THE ROW *IS* THE APPROVAL, and it must happen in the same commit as the code. There
# is no override flag, deliberately. The whole point is that a second owner arrives as a diff
# line with a note beside it instead of as an absence — which is exactly what $FFA4/$FFA5 was
# when P5.16's tc_map borrowed the framebuffer's MMU slots and nothing said so for six commits.
# ★★ "TWO OWNERS" below means the HAL writes it too. That is the condition that already cost
# this project a debugging round: $FF92/$FF93 share one set of interrupt latches, msys_player
# writes them and so does the HAL, and enabling FIRQ killed VBL — which presents as a timing
# bug, not as a contention. Ten registers are in that state today. They are not defects; they
# are the list that has to stay short and stay known.
# hot = per frame or faster.  P5.17 §3C, derived from the CALLING routine, not the line.
